title: Jenkins Examples
description: Small Jenkins examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Meet a pipeline
examples.description: A pipeline is a saved sequence of build or check steps. Jenkins can run it and keep a record of the result.

examples.title: Controllers and agents
examples.description: The Jenkins controller coordinates work. An agent is an environment where jobs can execute.
examples.code:
Controller: schedules and records jobs
Agent: runs the assigned build steps

examples.title: Stages show the journey
examples.description: A stage groups related steps under a clear name. This helps people see where a run failed.

examples.title: Shell steps need the right agent
examples.description: sh runs a shell command on a suitable Unix-like agent. Windows agents normally use a different step such as bat or powershell.

examples.title: Environment settings
examples.description: An environment block provides named values to the pipeline. Use it for ordinary configuration, not hard-coded secrets.

examples.title: Parameters let a person choose
examples.description: A parameter is an input supplied when a job is started. Treat input as data and validate it before using it.

examples.title: Conditions skip unneeded stages
examples.description: when controls whether a stage runs. It lets a pipeline state a clear condition rather than hiding it inside many shell commands.

examples.title: Always perform cleanup
examples.description: A post block can run after the main stages. always is useful for cleanup or reporting whether the run passed or failed.

examples.title: Bound a long-running step
examples.description: A timeout stops waiting after a chosen limit. It keeps stuck work from occupying an agent indefinitely.

examples.title: Parallel work needs independence
examples.description: Parallel branches can run independent checks at the same time. They should not accidentally change the same temporary files.

examples.title: Credentials stay outside source
examples.description: Jenkins can provide credentials through configured bindings. A job should request only what it needs and avoid printing secret values.
examples.code:
Jenkinsfile: names an approved credential binding
Credential store: holds the secret
Step: uses it for the authorised job only

examples.title: Read results honestly
examples.description: A Jenkins result reports the configured pipeline outcome. Useful reports explain what was actually checked and what still needs review.
examples.code:
Stage Check: completed
Configured checks: formatting only
Not checked: browser interactions
